description: Four rise-and-fall function generators with shapeable curves, plus a cascade section that plays them one after another, and a wall of outputs comparing and combining the four

params.text: Sets how long that channel takes to rise, 0.01 to 5 seconds before the speed switch multiplies it
Makes that channel run its rise and fall over and over instead of stopping after one pass; flicking it also starts a fresh pass
Sets how long that channel takes to fall, 0.01 to 5 seconds before the speed switch multiplies it
Chooses the order the cascade plays the four channels in: A, B, C, D in turn, or all four in a fresh random order each pass, or one at a time at random with repeats allowed
Starts all four channels and the cascade from the beginning of their cycles
Bends that channel's rise from logarithmic through linear at the centre to exponential
Bends that channel's fall from logarithmic through linear at the centre to exponential
Multiplies that channel's rise and fall times by five for slow, one for normal or a fifth for fast
Makes the cascade start a new pass as soon as it finishes one instead of stopping; flicking it also starts a fresh pass
Multiplies the cascade's rise and fall times by five for slow, one for normal or a fifth for fast, using the times of whichever channel it is playing

inputs.text: A rising edge past 1V starts that channel's rise and fall from the beginning
Multiplies that channel's rise time by its own voltage over ten, holding the result between 0.01 and 5 seconds, so the knob becomes an attenuator while a cable is here
Multiplies that channel's fall time by its own voltage over ten, holding the result between 0.01 and 5 seconds, so the knob becomes an attenuator while a cable is here
A rising edge past 1V starts all four channels and the cascade from the beginning of their cycles
A rising edge past 1V starts the cascade again from the beginning of its cycle, leaving the four channels where they are

outputs.text: That channel's function, at the range its own menu entry sets, either from zero up or swinging either side of zero
The cascade's function, one channel's rise and fall at a time, at the range its own menu entry sets
The lowest of the four channel functions, each scaled by its own range
The highest of the four channel functions, each scaled by its own range
The four channel functions added together and divided by four, each scaled by its own range
10V while the first of the two channels named on it is above the second, and 0V otherwise, comparing the raw functions before any range is applied
The distance between the two channels named on it, subtracted from the range that pair is set to, so it is largest when the two are together
The distance between the two channels named on it, so it is zero when the two are together and largest when they are furthest apart
The two highest of the four functions averaged, on a fixed 0V to 10V scale whatever the channel ranges are
The two lowest of the four functions averaged, on a fixed 0V to 10V scale whatever the channel ranges are
10V while that channel is rising and 0V otherwise
10V while that channel is falling and 0V otherwise
10V while the cascade is rising and 0V otherwise
10V while the cascade is falling and 0V otherwise

notes: the four channels come up with Loop switched on and a one second rise and fall, so the module runs as soon as it is added to a patch.
a cable in a rise or fall CV jack multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, so 0V there stops that stage at its shortest and 10V leaves the knob alone.
each channel, each pair section and the cascade has its own output range on the right-click menu, chosen from 1V, 2V, 3V, 5V and 10V, each either unipolar or swinging both ways.
the All Ranges submenu can override every one of those at once; switching the override off again puts back the settings each section had before.
the cascade plays only one channel at a time and takes its rise and fall times from that channel, so the cascade output is not a copy of any channel output.
the four lamps in the middle show which channel the cascade is playing and how far through it is.
this module is monophonic: every jack reads or writes one channel only.
